Spanish Wikipedia/Wikidata give -13.5704, -71.9957, 12.5 km from the stored point and about 6 km south of central Cusco, which contradicts every text placing Cheqollo north of the town of San Jerónimo; the MINCETUR inventory locates it only verbally and OSM has no node for it, so no two independent sources give the site's point.

Gran Saposoa is a cluster of ruins spread over some 1,000 ha along the Huabayacu valley; the only quotable points are English Wikipedia (-6.9568, -77.5420) and Spanish Wikipedia/Wikidata (-6.9875, -77.6078), one source family that disagrees with itself by 7.5 km and lies 2.4 and 9.8 km from the stored point; the MINCETUR/turismoperuano listing and the news reports give no coordinates, so no two independent sources fix the site's point.

The stored point (and the English Wikipedia coordinates) is the modern village of Vescia near Foligno in Umbria (GeoNames 3164496), a namesake 222 km from the Ausonian city. Pleiades calls ancient Vescia 'now unlocated'; Italian Wikipedia offers several candidate areas (Cellole/Sessa Aurunca, Monte Massico, Castelforte), and the only printed point (Wikidata, copied verbatim by ToposText with low confidence) has no independent second source. Held for the owner.

The site is a 15.5 km2 archaeological landscape; only Wikipedia (and pages copying it, such as Wikishire and Archaeolist) gives a central point, while English Heritage gives only a visitor point about 2.5 km away near the access car park, so no two independent sources can be quoted for one point within 1 km.

The stored point matches the English Wikipedia point (48°3′13″N 113°22′0″E, the pagoda on the east side of the walled city) and Wikidata gives another point 1.3 km to the west (48.056, 113.3496), but both are one source family; no independent readable source (heritage register, Megalithic Portal, tourism pages) prints coordinates for Kherlen Bars / Bars-Hot, so the point is held for the owner.

Wikipedia and Andina place Iskuqucha (Izcucocha) in La Oroya District, Yauli, Junin; Andina adds that it was recorded in the survey for La Oroya's water and sewer project. The Wikidata point lies in Huancavelica, 147 km away and outside the district, and the stored point is La Oroya town itself. The declaring resolution is paywalled on vLex, and no readable source prints the site's own point, so it is held for the owner.

The site is the Gradistea Muncelului-Cioclovina Natural Park, a 38,000 ha protected area; the park administration only gives its bounding box (45 26'-45 42' N, 23 05'-23 22' E), Wikipedia/Wikidata give a centre at 45.571, 23.231 (about 5.9 km from the stored point, which lies on a forest road inside the park), and no second independent source quotes a point for the park, so the point is held for the owner.

Only Wikidata prints a point for the ancient theatre on Fabrica hill in Nea Paphos; the OpenStreetMap outline has no quotable point, and neither GeoNames, ToposText, Pleiades nor the excavation's own pages give the theatre's coordinates, so two independent sources cannot be quoted.

The stored point is the original Sybaris at Sibari (Parco del Cavallo), a different site; Wikipedia states the exact location of Sybaris on the Traeis has not yet been found along the Trionto, and Treccani only names the river, so no source gives a point for this site.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Muyu Urqu (13°32′33″S 71°57′23″W, 22 m from the stored point); the OSM-based Mapcarta page gives latitude and longitude only on separate lines and the excavation literature gives no coordinates, so no second independent quotable point exists.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family (and Mapcarta/GeoNames and Archaeolist, which repeat its exact figures) gives a point for Ka'Kabish, 17.81611, -88.72972 near Indian Church, about 34.6 km from the stored point; no independent second source for the site's point could be found, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is the war memorial in Sotta village (OSM memorial node at 41.5452, 9.1957), not the site. Lanfranchi and Costa place the Poghjaredda complex on Monte Rotondu at the hamlet of Petralonga Filippi, and T4T35 and a geocache describe it on the upper part of Monte Rotondu between Petra Longa Filippi and Pianelli (IGN: summit 41.5717, 9.2019; hamlet 41.5695, 9.1931), where French Wikipedia's megalith list and the Commons photos of the two coffres give 41.5708, 9.1992; but that point is printed only by the Wikimedia family, and the only other printed point (IGN POI / T4T35 / Megalithic Portal, 41.5239, 9.1968) is marked approximate and lies 5 km south of Monte Rotondu, so no two independent sources can be quoted for the site's point.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Auquilohuagra (9°46′22″S 76°38′56″W, 1.6 km from the stored point); the MINCETUR inventory entry locates it only verbally (hilltop above the hamlet of Santa Cruz de Umpash, Cochamarca) and no OSM, GeoNames or register page with a quotable coordinate was found, so there is no second independent source.

The site is the tumulus necropolis (Krcevine) near the village of Ljuljaci; the only printed coordinates (Wikipedia/Wikidata) are the village's rounded point, and no source gives the necropolis's own point.

The stored point (51.5701, -3.4700, also GeoNames' 51.565009, -3.472019 for the hill Mynydd Maendy) is the moorland summit near Gilfach Goch, but the site is the Iron Age hillfort Maendy Camp / Mynydd Maendy Hillfort (Cadw GM099, Coflein NPRN 301331, grid SS9573095510), about 9 km north-north-west above Treorchy at c. 51.6487, -3.5086. Only the Wikipedia family (the List of hillforts in Wales and Wikidata) prints that point in a form that can be quoted; Cadw, Coflein and the Glamorgan-Gwent HER give grid references, and the Atlas of Hillforts, ancientmonuments.uk and the Modern Antiquarian could not be read. Two independent quotable sources cannot be given, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is the river's (near its source west of Pickering), while Kitson Clark (YAJ 30, 1931) places the excavated lake-dwelling 'nearly at the centre of the old lake', looking west towards Barugh, i.e. further downstream. The only record with the site's grid reference (Historic England research record 60325) refuses automated requests, so no two sources can be quoted for the site's point.

The stored point is the middle of the 200 km long Independence Fjord itself (a body of water), as given by Wikipedia and Wikidata for the fjord. The Palaeo-Eskimo remains named after the fjord are scattered along its shores, in southern Peary Land (Midsommersøerne, Jørgen Brønlund Fjord) and south of it; no source gives one point for a site called Independence Fjord.
